## Abstract

In this paper, we derive a pinching estimate for the traceless Ricci curvature in terms of scalar curvature and the ${C}^{1}$ norm of the Weyl tensor under the Laplacian ${G}_{2}$ flow for closed ${G}_{2}$ structures. Then we apply this estimate to study the long time existence of the Laplacian ${G}_{2}$ flow and prove that the ${C}^{1}$ norm of the Weyl tensor has to blow up at least at a certain rate under bounded scalar curvature.

## Introduction

In order to study a smooth 7-manifold M admitting a torsion-free ${G}_{2}$-structure, Bryant [1] introduced the following Laplacian ${G}_{2}$ flow for closed ${G}_{2}$-structure:$$\{\begin{array}{cc}\hfill {\partial }_{t}\phi (t)\phantom{\rule{0.2em}{0ex}}& ={\mathrm{\Delta }}_{\phi (t)}\phi (t),\hfill \\ \hfill \phi (0)\phantom{\rule{0.2em}{0ex}}& =\phi ,\hfill \end{array}$$ where ${\mathrm{\Delta }}_{\phi (t)}\phi (t)=d{d}_{\phi (t)}^{⁎}\phi (t)+{d}_{\phi (t)}^{⁎}d\phi (t)$ is the Hodge Laplacian of $g(t)$ and φ is an initial closed ${G}_{2}$-structure (a positive closed three-form). Here $g(t)$ is the Riemannian metric algebraically determined by $\phi (t)$. Since ${\mathrm{\Delta }}_{\phi }\phi =d{d}_{\phi }^{⁎}\phi $ for a closed ${G}_{2}$-structure φ, we see that the closedness of $\phi (t)$ is preserved along the Laplacian flow (1.1).

Abstract
    

## We prove a logarithmic Sobolev inequality along the G 2 -Laplacian flow. A uniform Sololev inequality along the G 2 -Laplacian flow with uniformly bounded scalar curvature is derived from the logarithmic Sobolev inequality. The uniform Sololev inequality implies a κ -noncollapsing estimate for the G 2 -Laplacian flow with uniformly bounded scalar curvature. Furthermore, by using the logarithmic Sobolev inequality, we prove Gaussian-type upper bounds for the heat kernel along the G 2 -Laplacian flow with uniformly bounded scalar curvature.

### Backward Pseudolocality of G2​-Laplacian Flow

Weiyong He, Longhuan Yan

In this paper, we establish a new estimate on the time-derivative of pointed Nash entropy and use it to give a new proof of backward pseudolocality for Ricci flow. The proof does not rely on Bamler's compactness theorem and structure theory concerning limits of Ricci flows. Our methods also work for other reasonable geometric flows, like the G 2​-Laplacian, at a scale depending on its deviation from Ricci flow and its scalar curvature.

### Pseudolocality of G2​-Laplacian Flow

Weiyong He, Longhuan Yan

In this paper, we give a new proof of Perelman's pseudolocality theorem for Ricci flow, which does not rely on Perelman's Harnack-type inequality. The key step is an estimate relating initial local μ-entropy to pointed Nash entropy at later spacetime points. The argument also works for other reasonable geometric flows, like the G 2​-Laplacian flow, at a scale depending on its deviation from Ricci flow and its scalar curvature lower bound. As a consequence, we can also prove the quantitative rigidity results concerning pointed Nash entropy due to Hein-Naber and Bamler for such geometric flows. In the appendix, we also show that the other results in Bamler's work (arXiv:2008.07093), when suitably modified, remain valid for Laplacian flow with bounded torsion. These include log-Sobolev/Poincaré inequality for conjugate heat kernel measure, heat kernel estimates, and dependence of the pointed Nash entropy on its basepoint.

## Progress summary

Open · progress reported

Finite cases have expanded through dimension seven, but the all-dimensional conjecture remains open.

Brady and McCammond conjectured in 2009 that the orthoscheme complex of the noncrossing partition lattice is $\mathrm{CAT}(0)$CAT(0) in every dimension, which would imply that all braid groups are $\mathrm{CAT}(0)$CAT(0) groups.

Known results

  * Brady and McCammond (2009): proved the conjecture for $5$5 strands and established several rank-$4$4 cases.
  * Haettel, Kielak, and Schwer (2013): proved that braid groups with at most $6$6 strands are $\mathrm{CAT}(0)$CAT(0), giving a partial answer to the conjecture.
  * A 2020 thesis claims the $7$7-strand braid group is $\mathrm{CAT}(0)$CAT(0), but this remains a finite-dimensional result.

October 20, 2026: $k$k-shuffle complexes

Chloé Postel-Vinay’s manuscript claims $\mathrm{CAT}(0)$CAT(0) for the new $k$k-shuffle braid-group complexes through dimension $7$7, with every higher-dimensional case conditional on the Brady–McCammond conjecture. This is progress on related complexes, not an all-dimensional proof of the conjecture, and the manuscript is unrefereed.

Current status (as of October 2026): The conjecture remains open in all dimensions; cases through dimension $7$7 are known, while the new higher-dimensional conclusion is conditional and unverified.

### Local and Global Blow Downs of Transport Twistor Space

> Jan Bohr ^{a}, François Monard ^{b} and Gabriel P. Paternain ^{c}

Received April 02, 2025, in final form April 20, 2026; Published online May 05, 2026 Abstract
Transport twistor spaces are degenerate complex $2$-dimensional manifolds $Z$ that complexify transport problems on Riemannian surfaces, appearing, e.g., in geometric inverse problems. This article considers maps $\beta\colon Z\to \mathbb{C}^2$ with a holomorphic blow-down structure that resolve the degeneracy of the complex structure and allow to gain insight into the complex geometry of $Z$. The main theorems provide global $\beta$-maps for constant curvature metrics and their perturbations and local $\beta$-maps for arbitrary metrics, thereby proving a version of the classical Newlander-Nirenberg theorem for degenerate complex structures.
Key words: transport twistor space; geometric inverse problems; holomorphic blow down structure; geodesic X-ray transform.

> Abstract:The braid spaces are defined as universal metric coverings of the standard complex spaces, branched over certain hyperplane arrangements. We describe a natural family of convex functions on braid spaces and use them to prove that braid spaces contain no geodesic loops. This statement is a consequence of the well-known conjecture that every braid space is CAT(0).

The prototypical example is the triple of
K¨ahler forms associated to a hyperK¨ahler metric. Donaldson has conjectured that when the 4-
manifold is compact any hypersymplectic triple can be deformed via a path of cohomologous
hypersymplectic triples to arrive at a hyperk¨ahler triple. This conjecture is a special case of a
“folklore” conjecture in symplectic geometry: a compact symplectic 4-manifold with c1 = 0 and
b+ = 3 is actually K¨ahler.
I will describe an approach to Donaldson’s conjecture which goes via G2 geometry. A hyper-
symplectic structure on a 4-manifold X deﬁnes a G2 structure on the 7-manifold T 3 × X. There
is a geometric ﬂow, called the G2-Laplacian ﬂow, which attempts to deform a given G2 structure
into one with vanishing torsion. This is the G2 analogue of Ricci ﬂow. Applying this ﬂow to
T 3 × X we get a ﬂow of hypersymplectic triples on X which attempt to deform the triple to a
hyperk¨ahler one. The main result of the talk - joint work with Chengjian Yao - is that if the scalar
curvature of T 3 × X is bounded along the ﬂow then a singularity cannot form. It is interesting
to note that this result is seemingly stronger than what is currently known for Ricci ﬂow with
bounded scalar curvature.
